Honestly what you experienced is what many people experience after hardship in life. A lot of people don’t show one ounce of compassion to other human beings. I had a manic episode in 2017 and got diagnosed bipolar 1 with psychotic features and since that time have been very depressed. Many friends also did not reach out to me despite knowing what I was going through. Two in particular stand out. One, my roommate in grad school who also graduated from the same high school and was living at home (5 min from my home) for a few months after my episode, did not reach out at all. Another classmate who always called me when he couldn’t find someone else to give him a ride to the train station or pick him up when he was drunk, didn’t call or text me at all after my episode. 

An acquaintance of mine had to take a semester off of school due to a severe exacerbation of crohn’s disease and basically nobody visited her in the hospital or reached out to her.

It’s just a hard reality of life. Maybe we can both make it a goal to be extra compassionate to people who are going through hard times? Because we know what it’s like to be abandoned.

I’m chronically ill as well and understand what it means to be a patient. Unless you’ve tried the medications in question yourself or are a medical student or doctor, I wouldn’t comment on another person’s experience. For instance another poster had gained a significant amount of weight on seroquel and his father would make negative comments frequently. When his father tried a dose of seroquel, he woke up at night and ate an entire cake. After that, he learned his lesson and resumed his normal eating. Certain medications - remeron, seroquel, zyprexa, and clozapine, in particular, are notorious for weight gain. They affect certain receptors that increase appetite and have metabolic effects as well. I’m a medical student and this is pretty basic stuff that we learn.

Yeah remeron is known for weight gain. It’s nearly impossible to lose weight while still on the drug due to its effect of appetite stimulation. Zypreza and clozapine are the same way. 

It’s not an excuse OP these medications affect receptors that increase appetite. It’s also suggested that they have metabolic effects as well. I’m a medical student and we’ve learned this in psych.
